summary.title: SkillNet: Create, Evaluate, and Connect AI Skills

setting_and_object.category: Infrastructure / Resource (open skill repository, ontology, evaluation protocol, and toolkit)

details: Agents lack a unified mechanism to consolidate episodic experience into durable, reusable skills, so they repeatedly 'reinvent the wheel'
Existing skill repositories/marketplaces rely on manual curation and only indirect (downstream-task) quality signals, leaving skills fragmented, redundant, and unvalidated

SkillNet: an open full-lifecycle skill infrastructure that (i) auto-creates skills from heterogeneous sources (execution trajectories, GitHub repos, documents, prompts) via LLM pipelines, (ii) evaluates each skill intrinsically along Safety, Completeness, Executability, Maintainability, Cost-awareness, and (iii) connects skills into a typed relation graph (similar_to, belong_to, compose_with, depend_on)

Skills are treated as a unified knowledge representation bridging natural-language procedural guidance and machine-executable logic, organized by a three-layer Skill Ontology (taxonomy, relation graph, skill packages)
Released as a curated repository (200k+ candidate, 150k+ curated skills), website/API, and the skillnet-ai Python library + CLI

Multi-stage pipeline: deduplication (directory structure + MD5 of SKILL.md), rule- and model-based filtering, categorization into 10 functional categories (Development, AIGC, Research, Science, Business, Testing, Productivity, Security, Lifestyle, Other) with fine-grained tags, then evaluation-gated admission
Sources: open internet/GitHub aggregation, in-house creation, community contributions (subject to same automated checks plus periodic manual audits)
Over 20 task-specific skill collections released, including ones built for academic benchmarks
Automated LLM-based evaluator with fine-grained rubrics; three-level grading per dimension (Good / Average / Poor)
Executability additionally validated empirically by running code/tool-invoking skills in sandboxes
Human validation: 200 randomly sampled skills blind-reviewed by three PhD-level annotators, agreement measured by MAE and quadratic weighted kappa
Environments: ALFWorld (seen/unseen), WebShop, ScienceWorld (seen/unseen), all POMDP text-based; metrics = average reward (R) and average steps (S)
Backbones: DeepSeek V3.2, Gemini 2.5 Pro, o4 Mini
Baselines: ReAct, ExpeL, and a random-expert-trajectory Few-Shot baseline
Benchmark-specific skill collections synthesized from ETO expert trajectories, with no overlap with seen/unseen test splits; agents dynamically select and activate skills at inference

Integration with the OpenClaw personal-agent framework using lazy metadata loading: pre-task skill search/download, analyze/evaluate auditing reports, and post-task consolidation of solutions into new skills
Illustrative prototype workflows for autonomous scientific discovery (scRNA-seq cleaning/clustering, pathway mapping, report generation) and large-codebase coding agents
Comparison table against ClawHub, SkillsMP, SkillHub, Skills.sh across positioning, automated creation, quality evaluation, relation analysis, distribution, and scale

key_findings.finding: Equipping agents with SkillNet skill collections substantially improves both task reward and execution efficiency across environments and backbones.
key_findings.evidence: Versus ReAct, average reward rises ~40% and interaction steps drop ~30%; e.g., Gemini 2.5 Pro on ALFWorld seen goes 60.00 to 91.43 R and 18.72 to 12.80 S, WebShop 31.66 to 53.02 R; DeepSeek V3.2 ScienceWorld seen 69.86 to 84.87 R. SkillNet also beats the experience-based ExpeL baseline on every environment/split reported.

key_findings.finding: Gains hold for both strong and weaker backbones and generalize to unseen splits, indicating skills add capability complementary to parametric knowledge.
key_findings.evidence: Reward gains of +15.7 R for o4 Mini and +28.5 R for Gemini 2.5 Pro; improvements are consistent across seen and unseen splits of ALFWorld and ScienceWorld (e.g., o4 Mini ALFWorld unseen 49.25 to 73.28 R).

key_findings.finding: The automated LLM-based multi-dimensional skill evaluator is closely aligned with expert human judgment, making large-scale intrinsic skill validation feasible.
key_findings.evidence: On 200 randomly sampled skills reviewed blind by three PhD-level annotators, MAE stays below 0.03 and quadratic weighted kappa reaches near-perfect (1.000) across all five dimensions.

key_findings.finding: Executability is the binding quality constraint in large open skill collections, whereas safety and maintainability are mostly satisfactory.
key_findings.evidence: Repository-wide quality distribution shows high proportions of Good ratings for Safety and Maintainability but a markedly larger fraction of Average ratings for Executability; of 200k+ aggregated candidate skills, only 150k+ survive multi-stage filtering and evaluation.
